newsitem.title: USA: White House economic nominee backs stronger growth.
newsitem.headline: White House economic nominee backs stronger growth.

text.p: Janet Yellen, who is set to leave the Federal Reserve for a top White House economic post, told her confirmation hearing Wednesday she would like to see U.S. economic growth pick up.

"I'm not satisfied with 2.5 percent growth and I don't think anybody should be satisfied with 2.5 percent growth," Yellen told the Senate Banking Committee. "I think we ought to be focusing on trying to pursue policies that raise that growth rate."

President Clinton nominated Yellen, 50, to replace Joseph Stiglitz as head of the Council of Economic Advisers. Yellen was a Clinton appointment to the Federal Reserve Board as a governor and still has 11 years left in her term.
Some senators praised her for being willing to leave the Fed for the rigours of public policy life.
Sen. Christopher Dodd, a Connecticut Democrat, said it was "remarkable" that Yellen had decided to leave the protection of the Federal Reserve Board to "step back into this fray."
He added: "I admire you immensely for doing this."
Yellen said she regretted leaving the Fed. "But I feel far better prepared to contribute to the work of the Council of Economic Advisers as a consequence of this prior experience," she said.

Senate Banking Committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato, a New York Republican, said he expected the panel would approve Yellen's nomination, which would then likely go to the full Senate for a vote next week.
"I am very pleased you will be taking on this important assignment," D'Amato told Yellen.
